# unique-field-without-unique-index

- Dialects: mysql, postgres, sqlite
- Default: on

## Why

The model promises that a field, or a combination of fields, never repeats, and the application relies on that when it looks a row up by it. Only a unique index or primary key makes the database refuse duplicates; a check in application code loses races between concurrent writers, and a plain index does not prevent anything.

## Fix

Keep the uniqueness in the model (a unique field, or a composite unique index over the fields) and regenerate the migration. Deduplicate existing rows first, or the unique index cannot be created.

## Exception

Uniqueness that is deliberately enforced elsewhere, for example by a partial or expression index the model cannot express, or soft-deleted rows that may repeat; write the reason down.

The same text is printed by `schemalens explain unique-field-without-unique-index`. An exclusion needs a written reason. Back to the [rule index](README.md).
